# How many solar watts for a 1,000Wh power station?

**About 200W of panel refills a 1,000Wh station in a day and a half of decent sun. About 300W does it in one good day. Plan on 600–700W or more to do it in one winter day.**

## The math

Panels rarely deliver their rated watts. Heat, sun angle and charging losses usually leave about **70–75%** of the label rating reaching the battery.

**Panel watts ≈ 1,000Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × 0.75)**

| Conditions | Peak sun hours | Panel needed for a one-day refill |
|---|---|---|
| Northern winter / cloudy | 2–3 | ~450–735W |
| Typical US day | 4–4.5 | ~300–340W |
| Summer / Southwest | 5–6 | ~230–300W |

Sources: [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/), [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)

Peak sun hours are not daylight hours. A 15-hour summer day usually equals only 4–6 peak sun hours ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)). A 200W panel on an average day puts back about 630Wh ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station)).

## Check your station's specs first

1. **Maximum solar input (watts).** Panels beyond this limit add little in full sun. If your station caps at 200W, it can't take 400W. Some extra panel still helps in weak light or cloud, because it reaches the cap earlier in the day and holds it longer.
2. **Input voltage range.** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside the station's range. This matters even more when you wire panels in series, because their voltages add. Too much voltage can damage the station.
3. **Connector.** Most panels use MC4 plugs. Stations take XT60, DC barrel or proprietary plugs, so make sure you have the right adapter.

If you'll run loads while charging, such as a fridge, size up. Net charging is solar input minus what you're drawing.
